name: v3.5.2 Pitch Detection Improvements
body:
What's new:

### Improved pitch detection

- Now applying proper linear interpolation; previous detections were often ~2-4Hz too high.
- Run the detection twice (start/end of file) and take the most confident value.
- Snap Pitch option to round values within .4 of 440Hz/432Hz to those values.
- Updated detection range from 424-448 to 431.2-448

Properly testing each pitch detection idea is extremely time-consuming and analyzing with AI allowed to finally find a few clear wins among dozens of failed ideas.

Detection is now more precise and more reliable. Combined with the previous conversion quality improvements, it can be worth re-converting your library.

### 432Hz Batch Converter

- Failed conversions show error message in tooltip
- AAC encoding "should" now work on MacOS, remains to test

### Yang Downloader

- It was still broken due to YouTube changes. It's now fixed.
- Added Cancel button for downloads.

name: v3.5 Converter432Hz Major Uplift
body:
v3.5 has been released!

All apps got package updates and minor changes, and the main focus of this release has been 432Hz Batch Converter

## Video Conversion

Up until now, there was no solution for 432Hz video playback with good quality, other than applying a fixed pitch-shift ratio in the media player which is pretty poor.

432Hz Batch Converter will now insert an extra audio stream with title '432Hz' into the source video file (when "Add stream to original file" is selected). This will allow you to switch between both audio versions at will, play 432Hz by default, and preserve the original audio. You can even run it again to add another frequency. It will be possible to view/clear all audio streams that were added by this software (not yet implemented).

Since it's a batch converter, you can point it to your video folder and they will all get the new audio stream without any video re-encoding. It's mostly a lossless operation (other than sometimes changing the video container).

**Video Conversion is a premium feature that requires a paid license.** Definitely worth it, and there's no other solution to this problem.

## Metadata preservation

All audio/video metadata will now be preserved. This includes album arts, captions, chapter markers, tags and other streams.

## Improved Codec Support

The addition of FFMPEG allows to support many more formats. The converter will now behave more predictably with many exotic formats.

## Other changes

- Help Icons to explain some features, across the various apps
- UI improvements

It has been reported that the MacOS build was no longer working since the previous release. I haven't looked into it yet. I'll release the MacOS version once the issue is resolved.

name: v3.4 Improved Quality
body:
After 2 years, version 3.4 is finally ready!

Ads have been removed, and audio quality has been slightly increased. Free version offers superior quality from the last release, and paid version allows pushing quality slightly further for audiophiles who want the very best without compromise.

What's new:
- Added SRC Quality parameter (1-8) in settings. It was previously set to 1 in the Player and 4 in the Converter. It's now set to 4 in the Player and 6 in the Converter, and can be set to 7 or 8 with a license.
- Fixed Yang Downloader that was broken since a long while.
- Updated from .NET 8 to .NET 11
- Updated from Avalonia 11 RC to Avalonia 12 (faster/lighter rendering)
- Fixed an issue where license would get lost in 432Hz Converter when pressing OK on advanced settings.
- Attempted to fix an issue where settings would sometimes get lost. Let me know if you see it happening again.

Plans for the future (with enough licenses sold to invest the time)
- Explore whether pitch detection can be improved. Pitch shifting is excellent, but pitch detection is where improvement could definitely be made.
- Allowing to convert videos to 432Hz, not just audios
- Yang Downloader: allow login to download premium content for higher quality audio/video. This is considerably more complex than it seems.
- 432Hz Player: create a better UI
- Mobile apps.

I just thought: audio quality is GREAT in 432Hz... but what about videos? I'm watching all videos with a much worse "regular" algorithm in the video player. Live playback with this algorithm would be very difficult to program. Probably the only option is to re-encode the audio in the video. Currently, the way to re-encode a video to 432Hz is when downloading it from YouTube with Yang Downloader. Otherwise, you can re-encode the audio of the video and then merge it back with the video (using ffmpeg or LosslessCut), but this will get very tedious to perform on a whole library.
